## Definitions

- [passage] If collection data is compressed (which is the [`default for WiredTiger`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/program/mongod.md#std-option-mongod.--wiredTigerCollectionBlockCompressor)), the storage size reflects the compressed size and may be smaller than the value for [`collStats.size`.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/collstats.md#mongodb-data-collStats.size) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/collStats.md#output · keywords: working set for time series, default for WiredTiger, collStats.size

## Structure and components

- [passage] A document that contains metrics on the WiredTiger **spill instance**. When MongoDB writes to disk to fulfill certain operations, it utilizes a separate WiredTiger instance, which contains its own in-memory cache. This separate cache isolates operations from the main WiredTiger cache. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/serverStatus.md#spillwiredtiger · keywords: working set for time series

- [passage] | Aspect | Atlas Core | Atlas Infinite | | --- | --- | --- | | Architecture | Compute and storage run on the same node. Each data-bearing node runs on a virtual machine with attached storage. | Compute and storage run as independent layers. MongoDB manages the storage layer separately from the compute nodes. | | Compute scaling | You change compute capacity by selecting a different cluster tier. Atlas restarts the cluster's nodes when you change the tier, with no downtime on dedicated clusters. | You scale the cluster tier independently of storage. Scaling doesn't move your data, so it is fast. | | Storage scaling | You scale storage capacity and IOPS independently of compute on dedicated clusters, up to the maximum for the cluster tier. To add capacity beyond that maximum, you scale to a higher tier. | Storage capacity increases automatically based on usage, independently of the cluster tier, without downtime. | | Horizontal scaling | You shard a cluster when its data approaches the storage capacity, and add workload-specific nodes, like read-only or analytics nodes, as needed. | Higher storage capacity means you can store up to 128TB on a single shard without sharding. Adding workload-specific nodes is much faster. | | Recovery | Atlas monitors your database regularly, and performs auto-healing if it discovers an issue. If it replaces a node, the new node performs an initial sync before it serves queries. | Atlas monitors your database regularly, and performs auto-healing if it discovers an issue. If it replaces a node, the new node immediately connects to the storage layer, with no need for an initial sync. | | Cloud provider and tier availability | Free clusters, Flex clusters, and dedicated cluster tiers, on AWS, Azure, and Google Cloud. | Public preview: `M10` through `M60` replica sets in supported AWS regions, with storage capacity up to 128 TB per replica set. | | Feature coverage | Supports the full Atlas feature set. | Some Atlas features aren't [supported during public preview.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/infinite/atlas-infinite-landing.md#std-label-atlas-infinite-availability) | — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/index.md#compare-editions · keywords: working set for time series, M10, M60

- [passage] Sharding distributes data across the shards in the cluster, allowing each shard to contain a subset of the total cluster data. As the data set grows, additional shards increase the storage capacity of the cluster. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/sharding/ · keywords: working set for time series

## Measurements and reference values

- [passage] - If your WiredTiger cache fill ratio regularly exceeds 90% — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/tutorial/build-indexes-on-replica-sets.md#about-this-task · keywords: working set for time series
- [passage] Manually run [metadata collection compaction](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/queryable-encryption/fundamentals/manage-collections.md#std-label-qe-metadata-compaction) when your metadata collections exceed 1 GB. Compaction decreases the size of the metadata collections associated with encrypted fields, and improves performance. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/queryable-encryption/reference/limitations.md#manual-metadata-collection-compaction · keywords: working set for time series

- [passage] To hold the additional representative queries, MongoDB 8.3 also increases the storage capacity for representative queries in query settings beyond the original 16 MB BSON document limit. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/setQuerySettings.md#set-query-settings-by-passing-in-a-query-shape-hash · keywords: working set for time series

## Comparisons and alternatives

- [passage] Horizontal Scaling involves dividing the system dataset and load over multiple servers, adding more servers to increase capacity as required. Each machine handles a subset of the overall workload, which can cost less than high-end hardware for a single machine. The trade-off is increased complexity in infrastructure and maintenance. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/sharding/ · keywords: working set for time series

## Facts and statements

- [passage] You can check the size of a metadata collection using [`mongosh`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/mongodb-shell.md#mongodb-binary-bin.mongosh) and running the [`db.collection.totalSize()`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/db.collection.totalsize.md#mongodb-method-db.collection.totalSize) command. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/queryable-encryption/fundamentals/manage-collections.md#running-metadata-compaction · keywords: working set for time series, mongosh, db.collection.totalSize()
- [passage] As you insert or update documents, the metadata collections change and grow. Metadata collection compaction empties the `ECOC` and reduces the size of the `ESC`. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/queryable-encryption/fundamentals/manage-collections.md#metadata-collection-compaction · keywords: working set for time series, ECOC, ESC
- [passage] In the worst case, running metadata compaction reveals the number of unique field/value pairs inserted across all documents since the previous compaction. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/queryable-encryption/fundamentals/manage-collections.md#scheduling-metadata-compaction · keywords: working set for time series
- [passage] For details on the exact information revealed by metadata compaction, see "Section 6: Theoretical Analysis" and "Section 9: Guidelines" in MongoDB's [Queryable Encryption Technical Paper](https://www.mongodb.com/collateral/queryable-encryption-technical-paper). — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/queryable-encryption/fundamentals/manage-collections.md#scheduling-metadata-compaction · keywords: working set for time series
- [passage] - `docinserts`: the number of documents inserted since the last compaction. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/queryable-encryption/fundamentals/manage-collections.md#scheduling-metadata-compaction · keywords: working set for time series, docinserts
- [passage] - `valinserts`: the number of unique field/value pairs inserted since the last compaction. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/queryable-encryption/fundamentals/manage-collections.md#scheduling-metadata-compaction · keywords: working set for time series, valinserts
- [passage] The number of encrypted fields per document multiplied by the number of insertions since last compaction, minus the number of unique field/value pairs inserted across all documents since the last compaction, should be greater than or equal to the number of documents to remove from the `ESC`. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/queryable-encryption/fundamentals/manage-collections.md#scheduling-metadata-compaction · keywords: working set for time series, ESC
- [passage] The formula would be satisfied, for example, if 200 documents were inserted since the last compaction with a total of 200 unique field/value pairs across all documents, or if 400 documents were inserted since the last compaction with 700 unique field/value pairs. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/queryable-encryption/fundamentals/manage-collections.md#example · keywords: working set for time series

- [passage] Database systems with large data sets or high throughput applications can challenge the capacity of a single server. For example, high query rates can exhaust the CPU capacity of the server. Working set sizes larger than the system's RAM stress the I/O capacity of disk drives. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/sharding/ · keywords: working set for time series
- [passage] Vertical Scaling increases the capacity of a single server by using a more powerful CPU, adding more RAM, or expanding storage. Available technology and cloud provider hardware configurations impose a practical maximum for vertical scaling. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/sharding/ · keywords: working set for time series
- [passage] Performance issues may indicate that the database is operating at capacity and that it is time to add additional capacity to the database. - [passage] Many concurrent application requests may overwhelm the server's ability to keep up with demand.
